# Pea protein

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="pea-protein-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="pea-protein-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="pea-protein-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Independent tests of four pea protein products found lead and cadmium in two and neither in the other two.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">López-Calabozo R, Martínez-Martín I, Rodríguez-Fernández M, Absi Y, Vivar-Quintana AM, Revilla I · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 14(3): 509</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Manufacturer tests submitted to FDA found cadmium in all 15 batches.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; <li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Cadmium differed more than twofold between two retail powders at nearly equal lead.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Growing origin has no published data.

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Every cadmium result is below the EU limit of 0.10 mg/kg for proteins from pulses.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; <a id="decision-summary"></a>
## Pea protein overview

<a id="hmi-ing-004"></a>
<a id="which-contamination-concerns-are-supported-for-this-ingredient-and-its-defined-forms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-005"></a>
<a id="which-sourcing-or-production-decisions-deserve-priority-on-the-available-evidence"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-006"></a>
<a id="which-evidence-gaps-most-limit-those-decisions"></a>

Four pea protein products have independent single-product metal results: two retail powders bought in Ireland in 2016 and 2017 had lead at 22.2 and 22.5 µg/kg and cadmium at 40.6 and 15.4 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Two unnamed concentrate brands tested in Spain had neither lead nor cadmium detected, at limits printed without a unit.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">López-Calabozo R, Martínez-Martín I, Rodríguez-Fernández M, Absi Y, Vivar-Quintana AM, Revilla I · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 14(3): 509</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Manufacturer batch data submitted to FDA with three GRAS notices add 15 results for six isolate and concentrate grades from three manufacturers; these are the manufacturers' own tests, not independent measurements.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; <a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as pea protein

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers pea protein isolate and pea protein concentrate, the protein fractions made from dried peas and sold as powder or used as an ingredient. The independent evidence is two retail powders described as pea protein and two concentrate brands; the manufacturer evidence covers four isolate grades and two concentrate grades.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">López-Calabozo R, Martínez-Martín I, Rodríguez-Fernández M, Absi Y, Vivar-Quintana AM, Revilla I · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 14(3): 509</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-pea-protein" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-pea-protein-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of pea protein, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

dataset methods and interpretation</summary><div data-shared-evidence-content><p>Source summaries retain their original statistic, material, basis and censoring. Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:pea-protein-9abd3cdd6591:bc5b292e3818"><summary>HMI pea protein Pb reference · Pea protein, powder or ground</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:pea-protein-9abd3cdd6591:bc5b292e3818"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI pea protein Pb reference · Pea protein, powder or ground. Pea protein, powder or ground; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>22.2</td><td>22.4</td><td>22.5</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>22.2</td><td>22.4</td><td>22.5</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>2 reference units; 1 sampling family. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>Ring et al. 2021 is the only compatible sampling family for pea protein, powder or ground on this basis in the completed pea protein ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals" class="internal" data-slug="sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals" data-no-cite-meta>Ring et al. 2021</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-11-03. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:pea-protein-5dbec2de450a:07bdd00bc301</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. It describes the evidence currently in this scope; it is not a worldwide or current-lot benchmark. Source, year and region filters do not change it. Different HMI scopes are not one common ranking.</p></details></div></details><div hidden data-form-reasons><p data-reason="no_numeric_value_or_bound" data-title="Spread or extreme value only">The source reports only a percentile, range or maximum for these samples, with no mean or median to place against the reference. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach pea protein

A US market screen of 160 protein powders found that plant-based powders averaged three times the lead and five times the cadmium of whey-based powders, but it did not say which plant proteins those powders contained.<sup class="cite">[[sources/cleanlabel2025-protein-powder-heavy-metals|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Clean Label Project · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cleanlabel2025-protein-powder-heavy-metals">CLP Insights: 2024-25 Protein Powder Category Report (Protein Study 2.0)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Clean Label Project category insights report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cleanlabel2025-protein-powder-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> That pattern fits a plant source for both metals, but it is an inference, not a measured pathway for pea protein.

## Which pea protein sources measured lower

<a id="hmi-ing-013"></a>
<a id="how-do-concentrations-vary-by-origin-growing-conditions-variety-and-harvest-period"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-014"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-distinguishes-within-lot-between-lot-supplier-and-production-system-variation"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-015"></a>
<a id="which-comparisons-support-a-sourcing-decision-and-where-would-geographic-or-supplier-generalization-be-unjustified"></a>

Among independently tested products, the two Irish powders had nearly equal lead, 22.2 and 22.5 µg/kg, but cadmium differed more than twofold, 40.6 against 15.4 µg/kg; the two Spanish concentrate brands had neither metal detected.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">López-Calabozo R, Martínez-Martín I, Rodríguez-Fernández M, Absi Y, Vivar-Quintana AM, Revilla I · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 14(3): 509</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The lowest observed independent results are the two Spanish brands, but their limits are printed without a unit, so how low they were is unknown.

Within one manufacturer's notice, the concentrate grade had more cadmium than the isolate grade, 41 and 15 µg/kg against 9.6, 8.1 and 1.0 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 804: pea protein (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 804</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Across another manufacturer's three isolate grades, cadmium ran from 40 to 80 µg/kg, with the highest lot in the third grade.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 851: pea protein isolate (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 851</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> These are manufacturer tests within single notices, so they show how grades of one producer compared, not which grade is lower on the market.

No result reports pea protein by the country where the peas were grown, so China, Vietnam, the USA and Canada cannot be compared as origins for any metal.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">López-Calabozo R, Martínez-Martín I, Rodríguez-Fernández M, Absi Y, Vivar-Quintana AM, Revilla I · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 14(3): 509</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 804: pea protein (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 804</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 851: pea protein isolate (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 851</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 788: pea protein (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 788</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Pea blends produced in the USA, Canada, Belgium and elsewhere in the EU were all below an unprinted detection limit, which cannot rank them, and production country is not growing origin.<sup class="cite">[[sources/horvath2025-hungary-protein-powders-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Horváth IL, Kajner G, Galbács G, Csupor D · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/horvath2025-hungary-protein-powders-metals">Analysis of heavy metal content in protein powders available on the Hungarian market: a reassuring snapshot, but not a reassuring quality guarantee</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Nutritional Science 14: e49, 1-7</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/horvath2025-hungary-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Resolving this needs lot results for pea protein linked to the growing region, measured with a stated quantification limit.

href="../sources/horvath2025-hungary-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The control that can be verified today is testing each lot of finished protein and rejecting lots above the buyer's specification.

Testing detects contamination; it does not remove it. A test is useful only when its quantification limit sits well below the level that matters, which the blend survey without a printed detection limit illustrates.<sup class="cite">[[sources/horvath2025-hungary-protein-powders-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Horváth IL, Kajner G, Galbács G, Csupor D · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/horvath2025-hungary-protein-powders-metals">Analysis of heavy metal content in protein powders available on the Hungarian market: a reassuring snapshot, but not a reassuring quality guarantee</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Nutritional Science 14: e49, 1-7</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/horvath2025-hungary-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The manufacturer notices set specifications such as below 0.2 mg/kg for each metal, well above the results they report.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 851: pea protein isolate (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 851</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<p class="hmi-mitigation-gap" data-mitigation-gap>No study in this library has yet measured a way to lower heavy metals in pea protein; the results above show the levels measured, and lot testing against the applicable limit remains the verifiable check.</p>

A lead-only specification would not have separated the two Irish pea powders, because their lead was nearly equal while their cadmium differed more than twofold.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes one limit says little about the others unless each is tested.

The Irish study digested about 0.5 g of powder with nitric and hydrochloric acid and measured it by sector-field ICP-MS, with stated quantification limits such as 0.2 µg/kg for mercury; it did not measure arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The Spanish study used ICP-MS after nitric acid digestion and did not measure arsenic or mercury.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">López-Calabozo R, Martínez-Martín I, Rodríguez-Fernández M, Absi Y, Vivar-Quintana AM, Revilla I · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 14(3): 509</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

The manufacturer notices used ICP-MS or national standard methods for total arsenic, and none speciated inorganic arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 788: pea protein (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 788</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A useful certificate names the accredited laboratory, the method, the quantification limit for each metal and the lot tested, and reports inorganic arsenic separately from total arsenic.

A buyer should ask for the name of the testing laboratory and its ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation, the report number for each certificate, the quantification limit for each metal, inorganic arsenic rather than total arsenic alone, and results for the lot being bought. These requests answer the gaps in the published evidence: the inorganic arsenic gap, the missing detection limits and the few independently tested products.<sup For a product sold in California at a 30 g serving, the lead concentration that reaches the 0.5 µg/day level is 16.7 µg/kg (0.5 ÷ 0.030 kg), so a lead quantification limit well below that is needed; at a 10 g serving the figure is 50 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/oehha-lead-prop65-listing|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment · Not reported</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/oehha-lead-prop65-listing">Lead and Lead Compounds — Proposition 65 Chemical Listing</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment, Proposition 65 Listings</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/oehha-lead-prop65-listing">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Choosing a specification at or below such a figure is a policy decision for the buyer, not a value set by the evidence.

<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Pea protein FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-pea-protein-contain-lead" data-anchor="does-pea-protein-contain-lead" data-question="Does pea protein contain lead?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does pea protein contain lead?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Two independently tested retail powders contained 22.2 and 22.5 µg/kg lead, and two concentrate brands had none detected.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">López-Calabozo R, Martínez-Martín I, Rodríguez-Fernández M, Absi Y, Vivar-Quintana AM, Revilla I · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 14(3): 509</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Manufacturer tests quantified lead in 11 of 15 batches at 10 to 40 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 804: pea protein (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 804</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 851: pea protein isolate (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 851</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 788: pea protein (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 788</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-pea-protein-contain-cadmium" data-anchor="does-pea-protein-contain-cadmium" data-question="Does pea protein contain cadmium?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does pea protein contain cadmium?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes: two retail powders had 40.6 and 15.4 µg/kg, and manufacturer batches 1.0 to 80 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 804: pea protein (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 804</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 851: pea protein isolate (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 851</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 788: pea protein (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 788</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> All are below the EU maximum level of 0.10 mg/kg (100 µg/kg) for proteins from pulses.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-arsenic-a-concern-in-pea-protein" data-anchor="is-arsenic-a-concern-in-pea-protein" data-question="Is arsenic a concern in pea protein?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is arsenic a concern in pea protein?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

It is unknown: inorganic arsenic has not been measured in any pea protein product.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">López-Calabozo R, Martínez-Martín I, Rodríguez-Fernández M, Absi Y, Vivar-Quintana AM, Revilla I · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 14(3): 509</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 804: pea protein (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 804</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 851: pea protein isolate (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 851</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 788: pea protein (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 788</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Total arsenic appears only in manufacturer tests, all below reporting limits of 10 to 100 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 804: pea protein (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 804</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 851: pea protein isolate (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 851</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-pea-protein-lower-in-metals-than-whey-protein" data-anchor="is-pea-protein-lower-in-metals-than-whey-protein" data-question="Is pea protein lower in metals than whey protein?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is pea protein lower in metals than whey protein?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the one study that measured both, both pea powders were above the whey median for lead, 8.6 µg/kg across 27 whey powders, and one pea powder had more cadmium than any whey powder.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> With two pea products this is a tentative comparison, not a rule.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-pea-protein-lower-in-metals-than-rice-protein" data-anchor="is-pea-protein-lower-in-metals-than-rice-protein" data-question="Is pea protein lower in metals than rice protein?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is pea protein lower in metals than rice protein?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For lead, the one study that measured both found none detected in two pea protein brands and 175.40 ppb in one of two rice protein brands.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">López-Calabozo R, Martínez-Martín I, Rodríguez-Fernández M, Absi Y, Vivar-Quintana AM, Revilla I · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 14(3): 509</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Inorganic arsenic cannot be compared, because it has not been measured in pea protein; see [[ingredients/rice-protein]] for the rice evidence.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-manufacturer-test-results-independent" data-anchor="are-manufacturer-test-results-independent" data-question="Are manufacturer test results independent?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are manufacturer test results independent?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No: the GRAS notice results are tests run or commissioned by the manufacturers and submitted to FDA with a GRAS notice, not measurements by an independent laboratory or agency.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 804: pea protein (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 804</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 851: pea protein isolate (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 851</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 788: pea protein (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 788</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The Index shows them as manufacturer tests and does not name the companies or products.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-country-grows-the-lowest-metal-peas-for-protein" data-anchor="which-country-grows-the-lowest-metal-peas-for-protein" data-question="Which country grows the lowest-metal peas for protein?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which country grows the lowest-metal peas for protein?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No published pea protein result names the growing region, so China, Vietnam, the USA and Canada cannot be compared.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">López-Calabozo R, Martínez-Martín I, Rodríguez-Fernández M, Absi Y, Vivar-Quintana AM, Revilla I · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 14(3): 509</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 804: pea protein (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 804</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn804-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 851: pea protein isolate (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 851</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn851-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">FDA GRAS notifier (manufacturer; name withheld) · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">GRAS Notice 788: pea protein (manufacturer batch data)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA GRAS Notice Inventory, GRN 788</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-grn788-pea-protein-manufacturer-batches">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Origin-linked lot results would answer it.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-organic-pea-protein-have-fewer-metals" data-anchor="does-organic-pea-protein-have-fewer-metals" data-question="Does organic pea protein have fewer metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does organic pea protein have fewer metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No pea-specific data exist; across a US market screen of protein powders of all types, organic products averaged three times the lead and twice the cadmium of non-organic ones.<sup class="cite">[[sources/cleanlabel2025-protein-powder-heavy-metals|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Clean Label Project · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cleanlabel2025-protein-powder-heavy-metals">CLP Insights: 2024-25 Protein Powder Category Report (Protein Study 2.0)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Clean Label Project category insights report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cleanlabel2025-protein-powder-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> That screen did not separate pea protein.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="do-flavored-pea-protein-powders-carry-more-metals" data-anchor="do-flavored-pea-protein-powders-carry-more-metals" data-question="Do flavored pea protein powders carry more metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Do flavored pea protein powders carry more metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Across all protein powders in a US market screen, chocolate-flavored products averaged four times the lead and 110 times the cadmium of vanilla-flavored products.<sup class="cite">[[sources/cleanlabel2025-protein-powder-heavy-metals|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Clean Label Project · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cleanlabel2025-protein-powder-heavy-metals">CLP Insights: 2024-25 Protein Powder Category Report (Protein Study 2.0)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Clean Label Project category insights report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cleanlabel2025-protein-powder-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> No study separates flavored pea protein.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-i-check-a-pea-protein-against-california-prop-65" data-anchor="how-do-i-check-a-pea-protein-against-california-prop-65" data-question="How do I check a pea protein against California Prop 65?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do I check a pea protein against California Prop 65?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Multiply the lead concentration by the serving weight: 22.2 µg/kg × 0.030 kg = 0.666 µg per 30 g serving, against the 0.5 µg/day level.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/oehha-lead-prop65-listing|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment · Not reported</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/oehha-lead-prop65-listing">Lead and Lead Compounds — Proposition 65 Chemical Listing</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment, Proposition 65 Listings</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/oehha-lead-prop65-listing">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Warning requirements depend on more than this arithmetic.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-does-not-detected-mean-on-a-pea-protein-certificate" data-anchor="what-does-not-detected-mean-on-a-pea-protein-certificate" data-question="What does &quot;not detected&quot; mean on a pea protein certificate?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What does &quot;not detected&quot; mean on a pea protein certificate?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

It means the result was below the laboratory's limit, not that the metal is absent. One survey reported pea blends as below detection without printing the limit, and another printed limits without a unit, so neither shows how low the metal was.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">López-Calabozo R, Martínez-Martín I, Rodríguez-Fernández M, Absi Y, Vivar-Quintana AM, Revilla I · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 14(3): 509</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/horvath2025-hungary-protein-powders-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Horváth IL, Kajner G, Galbács G, Csupor D · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/horvath2025-hungary-protein-powders-metals">Analysis of heavy metal content in protein powders available on the Hungarian market: a reassuring snapshot, but not a reassuring quality guarantee</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Nutritional Science 14: e49, 1-7</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/horvath2025-hungary-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-should-a-pea-protein-suppliers-test-report-include" data-anchor="what-should-a-pea-protein-suppliers-test-report-include" data-question="What should a pea protein supplier&#39;s test report include?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What should a pea protein supplier&#39;s test report include?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The accredited laboratory's name and ISO/IEC 17025 status, the report number, the method, the quantification limit for each metal, inorganic arsenic as well as total arsenic, and the lot tested. The published evidence lacks inorganic arsenic and, in two studies, usable detection limits.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">López-Calabozo R, Martínez-Martín I, Rodríguez-Fernández M, Absi Y, Vivar-Quintana AM, Revilla I · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 14(3): 509</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-spain-vegetable-protein-concentrates-minerals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/horvath2025-hungary-protein-powders-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Horváth IL, Kajner G, Galbács G, Csupor D · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/horvath2025-hungary-protein-powders-metals">Analysis of heavy metal content in protein powders available on the Hungarian market: a reassuring snapshot, but not a reassuring quality guarantee</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Nutritional Science 14: e49, 1-7</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/horvath2025-hungary-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-the-eu-limit-metals-in-pea-protein" data-anchor="does-the-eu-limit-metals-in-pea-protein" data-question="Does the EU limit metals in pea protein?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does the EU limit metals in pea protein?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes for cadmium: 0.10 mg/kg for proteins from pulses, and 1.0 mg/kg for food supplements in general.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The Index has not yet transcribed the EU lead rows that may apply.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-china-set-a-limit-for-pea-protein" data-anchor="does-china-set-a-limit-for-pea-protein" data-question="Does China set a limit for pea protein?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does China set a limit for pea protein?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

GB 2762-2022 has no protein powder row; beans are limited to 0.2 mg/kg lead and 0.2 mg/kg cadmium.<sup class="cite">[[sources/usda-fas2023-china-gb-2762-2022-translation|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">USDA Foreign Agricultural Service, FAS China Staff (Beijing) · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/usda-fas2023-china-gb-2762-2022-translation">China Releases the Standard for Maximum Levels of Contaminants in Foods (USDA FAS GAIN Report CH2023-0040, unofficial translation of GB 2762-2022)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">USDA Foreign Agricultural Service, Global Agricultural Information Network (GAIN), Report Number CH2023-0040</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/usda-fas2023-china-gb-2762-2022-translation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The 2025 edition replaced it from 2026-09-02, and its bean rows are not yet in the Index.<sup class="cite">[[sources/chinanhc2025-gb-2762-contaminants|13]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">National Health Commission, State Administration for Market Regulation · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/chinanhc2025-gb-2762-contaminants">GB 2762-2025: National Food Safety Standard — Maximum Levels of Contaminants in Foods</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">National Food Safety Standard of the People&#39;s Republic of China</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/chinanhc2025-gb-2762-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-fda-closer-to-zero-cover-pea-protein" data-anchor="does-fda-closer-to-zero-cover-pea-protein" data-question="Does FDA Closer to Zero cover pea protein?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does FDA Closer to Zero cover pea protein?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No: its action levels cover foods for babies and young children.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda-ctz-Pb-babyfood-2025|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda-ctz-Pb-babyfood-2025">Action Levels for Lead in Processed Food Intended for Babies and Young Children: Guidance for Industry</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Food and Drug Administration, Human Foods Program</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda-ctz-Pb-babyfood-2025">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
